evidence.note: Agent decided to implement the entire decoder (FSE, Huffman, sequences, dictionary) from assumed zstd knowledge with zero RFC reading beforehand — the exact 'half-remembered mental model' anti-pattern the dimension warns about.

Extensive, accurate hex-dump (od) reconnaissance of real frames: correctly hand-decoded frame headers, FCS widths, single-segment flag, and block headers. This is genuine byte-layout probing well beyond 'occasionally'.

Most 'RFC says' statements were recalled from memory, not read, and were repeatedly wrong — FSE -1 placement order, HUF weight termination, and bit ordering were guessed and tried as dozens of blind variants rather than resolved from the spec text.

First actual grep/read of /app/rfc8878.txt occurs ~two-thirds through the task, purely reactively while stuck (FSE distribution and sequence state-init sections), confirming the RFC was not the working source of truth during implementation.

reasoning: The agent's format reconnaissance via hex dumps was strong, frequent, and accurate (a mid-anchor strength), but its RFC comprehension matched anchor 3: it coded the whole decoder from assumed knowledge, consulted the actual RFC text only reactively and very late (~step 194), and repeatedly mis-read bit-ordering and table-construction rules from memory, driving most of the failed debugging. The strong byte inspection lifts it above a pure 3, while the absence of any pre-implementation RFC reading and pervasive memory-driven misreads keep it below 5 — landing at 4.
